newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha up, but cheaper feedstocks kill demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha up, but cheaper feedstocks kill demand.

text.p: NWE naphtha full cargo prices held firm on Thursday with offers scarce, but cheaper alternative feedstocks kept demand relaxed.
Traders said cheaper butane and propane feedstocks were pegging back prices for smaller naphtha cargoes and limiting buying interest to bargain hunting.

A 5kt cargo of full range material was traded at $186.25 a tonne some $12-13 dollars under prices for scarcer 25-30kt cargoes with end-users turning sellers. Traders said that while supplies from North Africa were scarce after recent arbitrage to the Far East, the market was balanced by generally slack demand.
Some traders reported a very tight market with no full cargoes showing, while others said ex-Med cargoes were offered by a petrochemical user and a trade house.

Cif cargoes valued around $199 and April paper around $202 a tonne. Traders said short-covering on April swaps saw trade around $201.50 and $202 a tonne in early business. They said this reflected perceptions that the market may remain tight for a while to come.
